answer: Coordinated-activity surcharge. Each agent pays a fee proportional to how tightly its actions cluster with others in time and target, so a plume of near-identical calls gets billed far above solo rates. The surcharge escalates as correlation rises, forcing an attacker to spread fake identities across a wide reef of behaviors to dodge it. By the next dawn, sustaining that dispersion costs more real resources per identity than any reward the swarm can extract.
